## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `a788fbfbf1176bc61f1b48f6e5969b2c3bb3956e`
Local-runs: none
Scope: skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md, skills/objectstack-data/evals/hooks-security-seeds-datasources.json, skills/objectstack-data/rules/relationships.md, skills/objectstack-data/rules/security.md + scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs
Security-touching: yes
Rule-change-verified: none

PR #37859 for card #37374, net diff against `main` (merge base `f19ae3a8`; `main` is now `adb65d16`, the PR reads mergeable, and no file of this diff's three skill texts moved on `main` since the base). Inputs read: the card body and its five comments, the PR body and six-file list, the net diff, the check-runs on this head, and the cited code on `origin/main`.

### ① Derived judgments

- Accept-set: none changes. No schema, no validator, no runtime code is in the diff; nothing an author may write is newly accepted or refused. Right.
- Public surface: four published skill texts under `skills/**` change what they teach about `viewAllRecords` / `modifyAllRecords`; the three eval `expected_output` strings follow. The `assertions` blocks of cases 20 and 37 are untouched, so no eval pass/fail criterion moved. Right.
- Gate table: `CEILINGS` in `scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs` lowers three rows (6801 to 6800, 4201 to 4181, 4340 to 4334). No row rises and no row is added. Read off the tree: relationships.md is 16723 bytes, ceil(16723/4) = 4181; security.md is 17335 bytes, ceil(17335/4) = 4334; the ai SKILL.md fell 27230 to 27225 bytes and its row falls by one, consistent with the stamp-line offset its row already carried. Right.
- Check-runs on this head. Completed and green: Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Check PR Size, Test UI, Dogfood Regression Gate, Plan Test Core shards, Auto Label, filter. No completed run is red. PENDING at the time of this record, so not judged: Test Core (1/10, 2/10, 3/10), Build Core, Live E2E UI, Type Check (debt ledger, consumer gates, workspace, source gates), Lint (docs and code guards, ESLint, CI release and engine gates, repo and tooling gates, PM dispatch-gates, and the three scoped jobs: query-options erasure, tooling self-tests, slot lookup and corpus). The ratchet gate and its self-test run inside the pending lint families; the row arithmetic above is this record's reading of the tree, the check-run's conclusion is still owed before landing.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/37374-skills-view-all-modify-all-open-no-field.md` bumps `@objectstack/skills` at `patch`. The diff publishes corrected prose and eval fixtures only, in the same 19 major whose behaviour PR #37371 already shipped, so patch is the level. `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` stand on the PR body, the changeset and the claim alike, and they agree with the diff: no declared capability is narrowed or widened by this PR, the narrowing itself landed with #37371. Check Changeset is green.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev flags: the report carries `open_questions: []`, `security_findings: none`, `out_of_scope_findings: []`. Nothing to escalate.
- The one scope widening the dev called out (`rules/security.md`, beyond the two files the card names) sits inside the claim's file surface ("any other `skills/**` sentence that teaches View All / Modify All as a field vote"). Accepted: the removed words named the two bits in a list of field votes, three lines of teaching away from "from v19 they open no field".
- Eval case 38 left unchanged: correct. It teaches Modify All lifting the owner-only delete floor on a `private` object, the record axis, and that still holds.
- Tier: the diff pairs `skills/**` with a gate script, so the low-risk skills arm does not apply on path grounds either; this record's `Security-touching: yes` keeps it at Tier H independently.
- SQL push-down: not applicable. No query, no id materialisation, no in-app join in the diff.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix, no should-fix.

Code read on `origin/main`: `PermissionEvaluator.getFieldPermissions` and `superuserBypassSets` (`packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/permission-evaluator.ts`), `fieldPermissionVote`, `holdsSuperuserBypass`, `viewAllFieldsReadVote` (`packages/core/src/security/effective-object-permissions.ts`), the write gate and `computeQueryGuardFieldPerms` (`packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-object-inputs.ts`), and `packages/lint/src/validate-rollup-source-visibility.ts`.

- `skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md`, pitfall 2. Holds. The field merge takes votes from declaring rows only, an edit vote only from a row with `editable: true`, and `viewAllFields` adds a read vote and never an edit vote; `holdsSuperuserBypass` is read by the row-level consumers alone. So a field row without `editable` is lifted by another held set's `editable: true` row and by nothing object-wide, and "Modify All is no such grant" is exact. Tried to break it with an admin agent holding Modify All plus the locking set: the write gate returns the field as forbidden, 403, as the sentence says.
- `skills/objectstack-data/rules/relationships.md`, roll-up visibility. Holds. The lint rule's own contract on `main` reads "`readable: false` hides the field, whatever object-wide bit the set holds", and inside one set the own row beats that set's `viewAllFields` (`declaresOwnReadMask`), so "mask the summary on that set" needs no precondition. The removed clause was false from 19.
- `skills/objectstack-data/evals/hooks-security-seeds-datasources.json`, case 20. Holds, and matches the sentence it evaluates; `must_contain` still demands the mask row.
- Same file, case 37. Holds. `foldFieldRequiredPermissions` runs after `getFieldPermissions` in both the query guard and the write gate, so `requiredPermissions` is strictest-wins over every field row and `viewAllFields`. The votes that re-open a `readable: false` row across sets are another set's `readable: true` row or another set's `viewAllFields` (the own-row exception is per set), exactly the two the new text lists. The prompt's Modify All is now a distractor and the expected output says so; `requiredPermissions` remains the right answer because field rows still union across sets.
- `skills/objectstack-data/rules/security.md`, high-sensitivity fields. Holds. The shortened list is the full set of field votes on `main`, and the file's Three axes bullet already says the two record bits open no field.
- Sweep at head: every remaining View All / Modify All sentence under `skills/**` is the record axis (security.md Three axes, the delete floor, the `viewAllRecords` posture bullet; relationships.md on a detail row with no master; objectstack-data SKILL.md on a queue move; eval cases 36 and 38). None says either bit opens, edits or re-opens a field. The card's acceptance is met.
- `scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs` (implementing file). Agrees with the contract: each lowered row equals the measurement of its file at this head, each carries its reason and byte counts, shrink-only.

Nits, no effect on correctness or the contract, left as accepted deviations (a fix in the script would move the head):
- nit: the trailing comments on two lowered rows now describe an earlier step, not the value beside them (`// -2 to the measurement (was 4203)` beside 4181; `// -18 (was 6824), then -5 A2′ (was 6806)` beside 6800). The new comment lines above each row carry the true history.
- nit: pitfall 2 does not say that an `editable: true` row carrying a `when` grants only on the rows its condition matches. The sentence was silent on this before the change too, and objectstack-data teaches `when`.

> 
> Inputs — these and nothing else:
>   · card #37374: its body and EVERY comment (rulings and earlier records included)
>   · PR #37859: its body, its file list, and the net diff against `main` at `a788fbfbf1176bc61f1b48f6e5969b2c3bb3956e`
>   · the check-runs on `a788fbfbf1176bc61f1b48f6e5969b2c3bb3956e`: their conclusions ARE the gate verdicts
> ⛔ Not the dispatch order, ⛔ not the dispatching seat's own conclusions — this brief is adversarial by design.
> 
> Scope — the paths `reviewFace` returns as `hits` on this PR's file list: skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md, skills/objectstack-data/evals/hooks-security-seeds-datasources.json, skills/objectstack-data/rules/relationships.md, skills/objectstack-data/rules/security.md;
>   plus every file IN THIS DIFF that directly implements or enforces them — the gate that enforces a rule, the code
>   a jsdoc or schema line describes, the validator a skill teaches — reviewed for agreement with the contract.
>   Widen it freely, ⛔ never below `hits`; the record's `Scope:` line names the implementing files apart from `hits`.
>   The rest of the diff (tests, unrelated modules, lockfiles, generated output, changesets) is the lane seat's
>   ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`, exactly as a standalone PR of those files.
>   ④ judges the `hits` files and those implementing files ONLY:
>   lockfiles, generated output, changesets and prose elsewhere in the PR are not reviewed;
>   code outside the diff is READ to judge them, never reviewed.
> 
> Security — a `hits` path sits on the low-risk skills arm: when the change teaches security, auth or permission
>   behaviour the path name doesn't show, the record says so and the seat adopting the record adds the `security` label.
>   The record says so on its `Security-touching:` line, and the arm lands on `no` alone: write `no` ONLY when no changed
>   hunk teaches permission, sharing, credential, token, authentication or other security behaviour, else `yes`.
> 
> ⛔ READ-ONLY. No worktree, no checkout, no build, no test run, no gate re-run, no ablation: the check-runs
>    on the head already answered every derived gate family, and a local run costs more than it returns.
>    If ONE probe is unavoidable, the record's `Local-runs:` line says `probe — REASON`; otherwise `none`.
>    Scratch space is `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user/166e2125-4268-552f-a555-2b7c43a99f0f/scratchpad/pr-37859/l2/` alone; nothing there you did not write this round is read.
> 
> Judge, in the record's own sections:
>   ① Derived judgments — every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, each named right or wrong.
>   ② Semver level — the changeset (or `skip-changeset`) matches what the diff publishes, and the `Clause-②:` line.
>   ③ Boundary flags — every dev flag and every `open_questions` entry answered, or escalated.
>      On every face, SQL push-down: a new id materialisation or in-app join where SQL could push down is a
>      finding unless a reason is given (AGENTS.md, Prime Directive 5: SQL first).
>   ④ Design judgment — for EVERY `hits` file: does the change hold against the code it cites and the
>      scenario it is accepted against? A skill file against the card's eval prompt and the spec it teaches
>      on `main`; a schema file against the ruling or ADR it implements and its first consumer; an ADR
>      against its first consumer and its execution plan. For EVERY implementing file in the diff: does the
>      code agree with the contract, sentence by sentence? Read the cited code in the live tree, and try to
>      break the design.
>      Grade each finding must-fix, should-fix or nit — a nit has no effect on correctness or the contract.
>      A must-fix is a FAIL; a must-fix or should-fix earns a delta review of its fix; nits alone end the round.
>      Spell a must-fix or should-fix with its id and grade, `S1 (should-fix) — …`, and a clean round as
>      `No must-fix, no should-fix.`: the queue guard reads a graded finding as OPEN on this head and
>      refuses the record; the delta record names those it closes by id alone, `S1: closed`.
>      A nit is fixed only on the prose faces, or left as an accepted deviation or a follow-up card: a fix
>      anywhere else moves the head, and this record no longer covers it.
>      ⛔ Judge the tree, never the PR body's account of it.
> Sign `Implemented-by:` with the dev's branch and `Reviewed-by:` with your session id — the value is the FIRST
> thing after each colon.
